title: Multiomic atlas with functional stratification and developmental dynamics of zebrafish cis-regulatory elements

items.section: Abstract
items.q: What gap does this paper address?
items.a: Zebrafish is widely used for development and disease modelling but, unlike other animal models, it had no systematic functional annotation programme. The authors set up the international DANIO-CODE consortium and a central repository to store and process zebrafish developmental functional genomic data.
items.info: The comparison programmes named are ENCODE, Roadmap Epigenome and modENCODE.

items.section: Abstract
items.q: What are the main outputs of the paper?
items.a: A Data Coordination Center with 1,802 unpublished and reanalysed datasets, and more than 140,000 cis-regulatory elements identified across development. The paper also shows that elements active at zygotic genome activation differ from those active during organogenesis, and it matches regulatory elements between zebrafish and mouse beyond sequence similarity.
items.info: The DCC is at danio-code.zfin.org.
items.concl: Zebrafish developmental genomics can be extended to mammals through comparison that does not depend on sequence alignment.

items.section: Introduction
items.q: Why was a zebrafish functional annotation effort needed even though zebrafish genomic studies already existed?
items.a: Separate zebrafish genomic datasets were largely out of reach for thousands of labs. Promoters and enhancers had been annotated for some adult tissues, but embryonic and larval stages, where most zebrafish research happens, had no functional annotation.
items.info: Zebrafish is used in more than 1,200 labs worldwide. DANIO-CODE started as a multinational bottom-up effort.

items.section: Introduction
items.q: What were the aims of DANIO-CODE?
items.a: (i) Collect published and new genomic data from 38 labs with standardised metadata. (ii) Build a single data coordination center (DCC). (iii) Develop standard pipelines and remap all sequencing data. (iv) Build an integrated track hub for common genome browsers.
items.info: Further aims were integrated analysis to classify functional elements and their developmental dynamics, and new methods for comparing zebrafish with mammalian genomic data.

items.section: Results - The DANIO-CODE Data Coordination Center
items.q: What data does the DCC contain?
items.a: 1,438 published datasets plus 366 datasets generated by consortium members to fill gaps. The new datasets are 15 CAGE-seq, 18 ChIP-seq, 11 ATAC-seq, 2 Hi-C and 320 4C-seq.
items.info: 1,438 + 366 = 1,804, which is slightly different from the 1,802 in the abstract. The paper does not explain the difference. Figure 1a summarises it as 1,802 samples, 38 stages, 38 labs and 19 assay types.

items.section: Results - The DANIO-CODE Data Coordination Center
items.q: How did they make datasets from different labs comparable?
items.a: All data were reprocessed from raw reads with standard pipelines: ENCODE pipelines for ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq, FANTOM for CAGE-seq, and the producers' pipelines for Hi-C, 4C-seq and other data. Quality and comparability checks were run within each data type.
items.info: Pipelines are on GitLab (gitlab.com/danio-code). Results are a public UCSC track hub that can also be uploaded to Ensembl, plus a WashU Epigenome Browser session. The DCC is updated periodically and is open for both download and upload.

items.section: Results - The DANIO-CODE Data Coordination Center
items.q: What is a PADRE?
items.a: A Predicted ATAC-seq-supported Developmental Regulatory Element. About 140,000 PADREs are in the track hub, annotated with ChromHMM chromatin-state categories.
items.info: These bulk-based predictions are supplemented with cell-type specificity from single-cell ATAC-seq.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: How did they improve transcript annotation?
items.a: Genome-wide transcriptome analyses annotate 5' UTRs poorly, so they used 139 developmental RNA-seq samples to identify 31,458 genes with 55,596 transcripts. These include 167 novel transcripts of uncertain coding potential (TUCP) and 726 lncRNA genes that are new to Ensembl and supported by CAGE.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: How many promoters did CAGE identify?
items.a: TSSs were mapped from 34 CAGE samples covering 16 developmental stages. On average each sample had 22,500 active promoters, corresponding to 16,303 genes, and 4,070 novel promoters were added to 18,461 previously annotated Ensembl TSSs (GRCz10).
items.info: They also curated 581 regulatory motifs representing 814 zebrafish TFs and predicted binding sites for them in all promoters.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: Why does an exact TSS position matter in practice?
items.a: Ensembl's RNA-seq-based TSSs were often far from the CAGE-defined TSSs, which affects guide RNA design. In dCas inhibition experiments, knockdown was more efficient when guides were designed against the dominant CAGE TSS rather than the Ensembl TSS.
items.info: Targeting promoters to block transcription can avoid genetic compensation triggered by mutant RNA, which can mask mutant phenotypes. Expression reduction fell as the distance between guide and dominant CAGE TSS increased. 26 genes were tested (Fig. 2c).
items.concl: CAGE is more accurate than the current Ensembl pipeline for promoter detection.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: How common are multi-promoter genes, and what do alternative promoters change?
items.a: They found 1,293 multi-promoter genes: 1,176 with one reference and one alternative promoter, and 117 with two or more alternative promoters. Of 978 transcript pairs with full CDS, 373 (38%) of the alternative promoters changed only the 5' UTR (e.g. dag1) and 605 changed the N-terminal protein sequence (e.g. bmp6).
items.info: Reference and alternative promoter pairs showed both convergent and divergent expression dynamics. Reference promoters were on average more highly expressed.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: Is alternative promoter use conserved in mouse?
items.a: Mouse CAGE data from comparable embryonic stages gave 1,779 multi-promoter genes. Of the 974 (75%) zebrafish multi-promoter genes with a mouse ortholog, 294 (30%) used alternative promoters in mouse. These orthologs were more likely to be expressed at similar stages (P = 2.7e-5) and highly likely to have multiple promoters in mouse (P = 3.24e-58, Fisher's exact test).
items.info: Multi-promoter genes were enriched in KEGG signalling pathways in both zebrafish and mouse.
items.concl: Alternative promoters in signal transduction-associated genes appear to be conserved across vertebrates.

items.section: Results - Transcript annotation and core promoter characterization
items.q: What is MARA, and what did it show?
items.a: Motif Activity Response Analysis models promoter expression dynamics from annotated TF binding sites to infer which TFs drive expression changes. Tead3 targets were upregulated from gastrulation onwards, Tgif1 targets were transiently downregulated, and NF-Y targets were downregulated from sphere stage onwards, consistent with the known activities of these TFs.
items.info: Tgif1 motif activity was anti-correlated with tgif1 mRNA (r = -0.92), supporting Tgif1 as a repressor. NF-Y motif activity correlated positively with nfyal (0.86) and negatively with nfya (-0.77), which suggests Nfya may replace Nfyal in the complex. The zebrafish annotation was added to the ISMARA webserver so any RNA-seq data can be analysed.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: How were PADREs defined and classified?
items.a: PADREs are reproducible ATAC-seq peaks from 4 pre-ZGA and 7 post-ZGA stages. They were then classified with ChromHMM using four histone marks at 5 post-ZGA stages.
items.info: The four marks are H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and H3K27me3.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: What did the UMAP of PADREs reveal?
items.a: It separated most ChromHMM functional classes, including promoters from enhancers. Near-symmetry around the y-axis reflected strand directionality, most clearly for promoters. Two clusters without chromatin marks were enriched for the CTCF motif with well-positioned flanking nucleosomes.
items.info: The method was developed to find known functional classes and possible new subclasses during development.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: How were enhancer predictions validated?
items.a: With two independent sets: enhancers with bidirectional eRNA signals called from nuclear CAGE, and a manually curated catalogue of published enhancers validated in transgenic reporter assays. Both co-localised with enhancer-classified PADREs on the UMAP.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: How does DNA methylation behave at PADREs?
items.a: CG-rich promoter PADREs stayed hypomethylated across all stages. Less CG-dense enhancer PADREs became gradually hypermethylated during development and were then hypomethylated in adult somatic tissue.
items.info: Dynamically methylated PADREs varied in when and how strongly methylation changed. For example, conserved phylotypic enhancers started becoming hypomethylated at Prim-5.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: Which PADRE classes are most evolutionarily conserved?
items.a: Early-acting enhancers were less conserved than enhancers activated later. Enhancers had higher average phastCons than promoters, and poised elements were the most conserved.
items.info: Conservation was measured by overlap with human CNEs and by cyprinid phastCons (grass carp, common carp, goldfish, zebrafish). Extended Data Fig. 5b also shows PADRE overlap with Mexican cavefish CNEs per stage. Wilcoxon P = 2.2e-16 for promoters vs enhancers and for enhancers vs Polycomb elements.
items.concl: Polycomb-bound enhancers may be a specific class important for differentiation and organogenesis, consistent with the hourglass model.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: How was cell-type specificity assigned to PADREs, and what did it show?
items.a: PADREs were integrated with Prim-5 single-cell ATAC-seq. PADREs active in CNS neural precursors had 3-fold more H3K27ac than those in differentiating neurons. Muscle PADREs had H3K27ac and H3K4me1 levels similar to neural precursors but different accessibility profiles.
items.info: Of 155 transgenically validated enhancers active at Prim-5, 117 had a cell-type assignment. In 72 (62%) of those, the scATAC annotation matched at least one activity domain of the transgenic reporter.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: What are cPADREs, and what temporal classes did they show?
items.a: Consensus PADREs are about 140k regions open in at least two neighbouring stages. Non-promoter cPADREs were clustered by accessibility into 16 SOM classes, for example class 4 (active early, then decommissioned), class 6 (active from ZGA onwards) and class 14 (late). Only the early elements lacked H3K27ac at their peak.
items.concl: Early and late enhancers have distinct chromatin and conservation profiles and form two separate classes of enhancers.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: What are COPEs?
items.a: Constitutive Orphan Predicted Elements: 2,109 regions that are open throughout development but carry no observed chromatin marks at any stage. They co-localised with constitutive SOM class 6, and 40% contained a CTCF motif.
items.info: Methods definition: constitutive distal PADREs (present at every stage) that are annotated as quiescent at every stage.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.q: What are DOPEs, and why are they interesting?
items.a: Dynamic Orphan Predicted Elements: 11,044 unmarked open regions that are open only at specific stages. Only 65 (0.6%) overlapped CAGE promoters. 2,513 carried active marks later in adult tissues but were already as open as active enhancers in the embryo.
items.info: Methods definition: cPADREs annotated as quiescent at every stage. They are called adult-marked DOPEs if they overlap H3K27ac regions in any adult tissue.
items.concl: Their opening precedes, or is uncoupled from, enhancer histone mark deposition, so they may be a previously unknown subtype of primed enhancers.

items.section: Results - Developmental specialization of Pol II gene promoters
items.q: How were Pol II promoters classified by chromatin architecture?
items.a: CAGE-defined promoters at Dome and Prim-5 were clustered by nucleosome-resolution ATAC accessibility into 8 classes. Similar clusters were found in human embryonic stem cells, which indicates the architecture classes are conserved.
items.info: The 8 classes are upstream offset, double NFR, wide, strong open, medium zygotic, narrow, medium constitutive and weak open.

items.section: Results - Developmental specialization of Pol II gene promoters
items.q: How do the promoter classes differ?
items.a: Mainly in their upstream configuration: width of the nucleosome-free region (NFR), strength of the central NFR signal, and presence of upstream open regions, all of which followed GC content. They also differed in histone marks, and every class except weak open produced antisense transcription (PROMPTs).
items.info: Medium constitutive and weak open differed only in NFR amplitude. Weak open could reflect lower promoter activity or activity in only a subset of cells. Double NFR, wide and upstream offset had CAGE signal from both the main NFR and an upstream region, with sense stronger than antisense.

items.section: Results - Developmental specialization of Pol II gene promoters
items.q: Are promoter classes stable over development, and are they linked to particular gene sets?
items.a: Classes stayed stable from Dome to Prim-5, so they seem to reflect distinct regulatory mechanisms rather than stage-dependent activity states. Wide and strong open had the most conserved promoters and were enriched for transcription regulator genes. Double NFR was enriched for maternally expressed genes, while weak open and medium zygotic were mainly early and late zygotic respectively.
items.info: Each class also had its own GO enrichment categories.
items.concl: Promoter classes show functional specialisation and are conserved across vertebrates.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.q: What are GRBs and bystander genes?
items.a: Genomic regulatory blocks are regions where many long-range enhancers of key developmental genes overlap highly conserved noncoding elements (HCNEs). They also contain bystander genes that do not respond to those enhancers, and GRB extent coincides with the TADs around developmental genes.
items.info: GRB TADs have a high density of extreme noncoding conservation. Non-GRB TADs do not.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.q: How does chromatin opening differ between GRB and non-GRB TADs?
items.a: TAD boundaries (as defined in late Long-pec embryos) began opening as early as Dome and stayed open. Accessibility rose strongly across the whole TAD in GRB TADs, but only mildly and later in non-GRB TADs.
items.info: TADs started forming early but were fully formed only at later stages. Promoter-proximal enhancers were more common early and distal enhancers late.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.q: What are H3K27ac ensembles?
items.a: Clusters of early-active (Dome stage) PADREs joined by uninterrupted H3K27ac signal. About 1,600 were detected, about 1,300 of them in TADs, and they were enriched in GRB TADs.
items.info: They resemble super-enhancers but are more numerous (231 super-enhancers reported in mouse and 411 in zebrafish) and appear early, before lineage determination. They were called with the ROSE algorithm on Dome-stage H3K27ac with TSS exclusion set to 500 bp.
items.concl: Because of their scale and early appearance, they are treated as distinct from super-enhancers.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.q: What features link H3K27ac ensembles to chromatin topology?
items.a: Promoters were enriched at ensemble boundaries, and ensembles contained most early enhancer PADREs. At Dome there were more Hi-C contacts within ensembles; by Prim-5 strong contacts spread across the whole TAD and H3K27ac narrowed to individual PADRE peaks. TADs with Dome ensembles were in the active A-compartment at Prim-5.
items.info: In GRB TADs, H3K27ac spread from the ensembles to fill the whole TAD at later stages. Late-only PADREs were long-range enhancers spread across the TAD and were not enriched in ensembles.
items.concl: Ensembles may help open chromatin in their host TADs on time.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.q: How do ensembles relate to gene expression?
items.a: Ensemble-associated promoters fell mostly into SOM clusters with peak expression in early post-ZGA stages: the Blastula-Gastrula Transition (BGT) and Gastrula-Segmentation Transition (GST) classes. GRB target genes associated with ensembles were expressed earlier than other GRB target genes.
items.info: GRB TADs mainly contain ubiquitously expressed bystanders and late zygotic target genes. The BGT class appeared only in GRB TADs with an ensemble.
items.concl: Ensembles help activate early developmental genes. A target gene not in contact with an ensemble is expressed only once long-range interactions are in place.

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.q: Why did they need a new method to compare zebrafish and mouse regulatory elements?
items.a: Existing methods depend on direct alignment, but noncoding sequence similarity is lost over the large fish-mammal distance. The new method uses the fact that functional elements often keep collinear syntenic positions while their spacing scales with genome size, especially in GRB TADs.
items.info: 13 high-quality bridging species genomes and stepped pairwise alignments give multi-species anchors. Syntenic positions are then interpolated between anchors.

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.q: How much did the multi-species approach improve mapping?
items.a: GRB TADs were defined as the 1,000 TADs with the highest CNE density, split into 1-kb bins, and the bin centres were mapped from zebrafish to mouse. Compared with direct alignment, the multi-species approach cut the distance from bin centres to the nearest anchor 16-fold in zebrafish and 29-fold in mouse.
items.info: Zebrafish and mouse GRB TADs differ about two-fold in size. Fig. 6b used n = 528,830 bin centres.

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.q: Is H3K27me3 distribution conserved between zebrafish and mouse?
items.a: Using phylotypic stages (zebrafish Prim-5, mouse E10.5), shared H3K27me3 enrichment was significantly more likely in both directly alignable and non-alignable regions, for example at the irx3a locus without direct sequence conservation. Some TADs, such as those with her9 or celf5a, showed more species-specific signal.
items.info: Extended Data Fig. 10e: alignable bins n = 22,403 and non-alignable n = 97,767, both P < 2.2e-16. Shuffled control P = 0.39 (Fisher's exact test). Mouse data were merged from 6 tissues (fore-, mid-, hindbrain, facial prominence, heart, limb) to create a virtual embryo, and the signal was quantile-normalised.
items.concl: Epigenomic subdomains can be conserved in location and span without sequence conservation.

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.q: What are DC, IC and NC elements, and how conserved are they functionally?
items.a: Zebrafish ATAC peaks in GRB TADs were classed as directly conserved (DC, in direct alignment with mouse: 16,188, 11.5%), indirectly conserved (IC, alignable only through bridging species: 6,137, 4.4%) or non-conserved (NC). DC and IC elements shared DNase hypersensitivity, ChromHMM state and TFBS motifs with their mouse counterparts more than NC elements did.
items.info: The IC count is 6,137 in the text but 6,173 in Fig. 6f, which also gives 118,272 NC peaks. Methods: IC means projected with score > 0.99, i.e. a summed distance to anchors under 150 bp along the optimal species path.
items.concl: IC elements are functionally conserved to a similar degree as DC elements even though they cannot be aligned directly.

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.q: Are H3K27ac ensembles conserved in mouse?
items.a: Yes. Mouse H3K27ac signal was significantly enriched within the projected zebrafish ensembles (P < 2.2e-16, Fisher's exact test).
items.info: Bins compared: n = 11,083 within and 93,020 outside ensembles, with enrichment defined as signal at or above the 80th percentile. Example: the ensemble next to the zebrafish aktip gene. Mouse data were previously published.
items.concl: Ensembles appear to be evolutionarily conserved epigenetic subdomains in vertebrates.

items.section: Discussion
items.q: What do the authors suggest H3K27ac ensembles do?
items.a: They propose that ensembles organise nuclear topology as local interaction hubs around early active loci while TADs are first forming. They describe ensembles as distinct from super-enhancers that target lineage-determining genes.
items.info: This is a proposed model based on correlation. The paper does not test it functionally.

items.section: Discussion
items.q: What are the main limitations?
items.a: All datasets are bulk whole-embryo samples, which can hide chromatin dynamics of rare cell populations or different cell-cycle states. Enhancer marks from small cell numbers may also be lost through thresholding.
items.info: The authors argue that comparing intersections of independent chromatin features reduces averaging artefacts. They note COPEs and DOPEs may carry histone marks that have not been mapped yet.
items.concl: More single-cell data will be needed to further stratify cis-regulatory classes.

items.section: Discussion
items.q: What practical uses do the authors foresee for the resource?
items.a: A foundation for single-cell transcriptome and open-chromatin studies, and targeted manipulation of genomic elements. The high-resolution promoter annotation can guide reagent design for gene regulation assays, transgenic cell labelling and transcription blocking.
items.info: The anchoring approach also lets zebrafish annotations add to mammalian and modENCODE functional maps.

items.section: Methods - Data collection
items.q: How were data collected and annotated in the DCC?
items.a: Community members uploaded demultiplexed FASTQ files and annotated them through the DCC web interface. Curators added strategically selected published datasets for under-represented stages or assays.
items.info: The data model is derived from SRA data structures and uses controlled vocabularies based on ZFIN nomenclature. Workflows ran on DNAnexus, and data freezes keep snapshots as new data are added.

items.section: Methods - Transcripts identification
items.q: Which pipeline was used to identify transcripts?
items.a: Wild-type paired-end stranded RNA-seq (6 datasets selected from 528) was aligned to GRCz10 with STAR v2.5.1b. Transcripts were called with StringTie v1.33b, merged with TACO (194,508 transcripts) and quantified with Salmon v0.11.2.
items.info: Filters removed read-through and mono-exonic transcripts and those overlapping 3 or more Ensembl genes. Protein-coding transcripts over 200 kb and lncRNAs over 100 kb were excluded. Robust set = expressed in at least 2 closest stages. CAGE TCs within 500 bp were also considered, giving 70,354 permissive and 55,596 robust transcripts, which cover 23,568 and 22,065 of 35,117 Ensembl v91 genes. Exactly how the CAGE step defines the sets is worded unclearly.

items.section: Methods - Promoterome construction
items.q: How did they handle differences between CAGE protocols?
items.a: nAnTi CAGE samples had more signal from annotated exons (exon painting, attributed to recapping of degraded mRNAs) and more initiation at non-YC/YR dinucleotides than tagging CAGE. All CAGE tags not initiated at YC or YR dinucleotides were removed.
items.info: Signal was power-law normalised (alpha = 1.1, fit range 5 to 1,000 tags). CAGEr settings: threshold 0.7 TPM, distclu, maxDist 20, singletons removed unless above 5. Consensus clusters (tpmThreshold 1, maxDist 20) had to be expressed at 1 TPM or more in at least 2 consecutive stages, giving 27,781 consensus clusters.

items.section: Methods - Annotation of alternative transcript and alternative promoter
items.q: How were reference and alternative promoters defined?
items.a: As in Ensembl, the longest CAGE-supported transcript is the reference transcript and its promoter is the reference promoter. Transcripts with TSSs within 300 nt were excluded; the longest remaining distal transcript became an alternative transcript, and the process was repeated.
items.info: Transcript models came from Ensembl, RefSeq and DANIO-CODE RNA-seq. Mouse used FANTOM5 CAGE at E11 to E14 and the Ensembl ortholog table.

items.section: Methods - Motif activity analysis
items.q: How was the zebrafish motif set built and TFBSs predicted?
items.a: Zebrafish DNA-binding domains were found with HMMER and Pfam models, then aligned with BLAT to human and mouse DBDs with known motifs, assigning 814 zebrafish TFs to 581 motifs. TFBSs were predicted with MotEvo in promoter regions (500 bp either side of the CAGE TSR) aligned to goldfish, common carp and grass carp.
items.info: Orthologous regions were found with LAST and aligned with T-Coffee. Motifs whose site counts correlated above r = 0.6 were merged into 489 motif groups, and ISMARA was run on the CAGE time course.

items.section: Methods - Functional segmentation of the genome
items.q: How was ChromHMM set up and which states were defined?
items.a: ChromHMM was run on H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and H3K27me3 at Dome, 75%-epiboly, 5-9 somites, Prim-5 and Long-pec. They found 10 optimal states, labelled by reference to Roadmap: 2 active TSS, 2 TSS flanking, active enhancer, enhancer flanking, primed enhancer, poised, Polycomb repressed and quiescent.
items.info: Active enhancer = strong H3K27ac and H3K4me1 without H3K4me3. Primed = H3K4me1 only. Poised = H3K27me3 together with active marks. Most of the genome carries no marks. New data were generated for 5-9 somites and Long-pec.

items.section: Methods - PADREs
items.q: How exactly were PADREs called, and why not call them cCREs?
items.a: Stage-specific open regions were kept if consistent between replicates (IDR < 0.1). The authors used a new name rather than ENCODE cCREs because PADREs include open regions without functional marks and to emphasise the developmental focus.
items.info: The permissive cPADRE set (all PADREs merged) has about 240k elements. The strict set (open in at least 2 neighbouring stages) has about 140k and was used for all cPADRE analyses. New ATAC data were produced for the pre-ZGA stages and 30%-epiboly.

items.section: Methods - UMAP visualization
items.q: How was the UMAP feature matrix built?
items.a: Each ATAC peak summit was extended 750 bp each way and split into 13 bins. ATAC, H3K4me3, H3K27ac and H3K4me1 tags plus NucleoATAC nucleosome signal were counted per bin, standardised, concatenated into 65 features and reduced to 2 dimensions with UMAP.
items.info: Nucleosome signal was included because some factors, such as CTCF, have well-positioned nucleosomes around their sites.

items.section: Methods - Promoter classification by open chromatin
items.q: How were promoter architecture classes computed?
items.a: For each TSR, the dominant TSS (highest mean post-MBT expression, at least 0.2 TPM) was the reference, leaving 21,914 promoters. Prim-5 ATAC Tn5 cut sites were Gaussian-smoothed (SD 3 bp), log-transformed and clustered with k-means (k = 8) within 800 bp of the dominant TSS.
items.info: Post-MBT expression was measured from Shield to Long-pec.

items.section: Methods - Genomic coordinate projection
items.q: How does the multi-species projection choose bridging species?
items.a: A non-alignable position is projected by interpolating between two alignable anchors. Each species gets a score that decays exponentially with distance to the nearest anchor, scaled by genome size, and the best combination of bridging species is the shortest path through a 15-species graph, found with Dijkstra's algorithm.
items.info: The scaling factor comes from a distance half-life, the distance at which the score is 0.5. Path length = 1 minus the product of the scores. The 15 species include zebrafish and mouse plus bridging species such as Xenopus, spotted gar, chicken, human, medaka and carps.

items.section: Results - Classification of genomic regulatory regions in development
items.text: DOPEs and COPEs are open with no detected histone marks. Do they carry unmapped marks, or is opening really uncoupled from mark deposition? Also, Extended Data Fig. 5b gives per-stage PADRE overlap with Mexican cavefish CNEs, worth going back to for Astyanax regulatory work.

items.section: Results - Developmental dynamics and locus organization of enhancers
items.text: Do H3K27ac ensembles cause early TAD formation and early target-gene activation, or only coincide with them? The evidence is correlative (Hi-C contacts, compartments, expression timing).

items.section: Results - Functional conservation of epigenetic subdomains
items.text: The anchor-based synteny projection (bridging species, shortest path) could in principle map regulatory elements between distant fish such as Astyanax and zebrafish. How well does the IC class hold up with functional tests, not just shared chromatin features?
